reviews.review:
Mass Effect 3 can easily be described in one word: stupid. The dialog and plot, gameplay changes, companion choices, and even the star chart are changed for the worse. All of the good things from the first game have been imported and made worse, while anything (good or bad) from the second game has been forgotten, butchered, or relegated to cameos. Even though the combat is greatly improved, that isn't enough to carry the campaign's awful writing. Mass Effect 1 & 2 both have elements that can turn away potential fans, but I don't see how anyone can say that this is their favorite in the trilogy.

Both the actual story and the dialog are terribly written here. A lot of the dialog feels like placeholder; Shepard has always been a charismatic orator, a mortal superhero for the rest of the human race to aspire to, and yet here a lot of Shep's dialog feels way too casual. Replying to heartfelt lines from other characters with dumb quips just makes it feel like they rushed through dialog production and went with the first draft. The intro mission on Earth is the only part that feels "Mass Effect" to me; almost everything else in the main story feels like padding, menial side quests that should be relegated to literally anyone else other than the savior of the galaxy. I could write a whole review about the other problems with the writing, but its best summed up as dumb over-explaining. We don't need to know where the Reapers came from or their motives, just leave it as a vague existential threat like the first game.

This whole game should've taken place on Earth, "Independence Day"-style, where humanity bands together to find a non-space magic way to defeat the Reapers. There would still be room for sequels, with humanity scouring the galaxy to fight back against the invasion and earn the other races' trust. Instead, your previous human ally Cerberus is turned into the boogeyman hiding around every corner, and you spend as much time fighting them as the other races combined. Although the enemy variety is best in this sequel, it tends to feel more "Shadowrun" than "Mass Effect" because of the new enemy's art direction.

Gone are the morally-grey companions Cerberus helped you find in ME2 and your relationships with them. There are only seven squad members possible (including Kaiden/Ashley), depending on your actions in the previous games, and all of the returning members are from the first game. All of the ME2 companions are either relegated to cameos or killed off in yet another poorly animated, poorly shot cutscene. Certain companions are important for parts of the plot and should've been possible squad members, but I can only assume the game's development was too rushed to implement content from the second game while it was still in development (ME3's development started during ME2). 

A lot of content from 2 was gutted actually, especially exploration and scanning: instead of dropping probes, you now just ping space sonar while flying around, and run for your life if you trigger a Reaper invasion. Reapers are embarrassingly a non-threat on the star chart and are yet another thing that feels placeholder. If you get caught by one, it just gives you a generic "critical mission failure" game over screen and you reload a save. There's no longer any resources for research to be found like in 2 either. Scanning just finds war assets, credits, or fuel now, and even then fuel doesn't really matter because you'll auto-pilot to the nearest mass relay if you run out.

Then there's the problem with the Reapers and the writing behind them. In the first game, it is implied that Sovereign is able to be defeated because Saren's second death caused some kind of internal damage to the Reaper. In this game, they just resort to throwing the kitchen sink at Reapers, hoping something will damage them, until Shepard has the bright idea of shooting them in the charging laser eyeball. No kind of power level is ever delineated; If these are hyper advanced AIs with superior ancient technology that have lived in deep space for 50,000 years, why would space machine guns work on them? They're supposed to be some kind of interstellar existential threat, and yet every race in the galaxy just throws their military forces against them, while refusing to cooperate towards a solution (without Shepard's help of course).

Despite the upper staff remaining mostly the same, even the art direction has taken a hit in this game. The first game used a lot of cool color temperatures, especially blues, with oranges and reds for highlights. The second game used a lot of warm color temps, especially oranges, with blues and greens for highlights. What did they do for the grand finale? They just blew out the contrast and saturation with zero thought into lighting, art direction, or cinematography. This looks, feels, and plays like modern slop except it came out 13 years ago. This can't be blamed on Marvel or JJ Abrams because this came out before the first Avengers movie and only the first Nu-Star Trek movie came out before it. Maybe there's something in the water that just culturally destroyed our brains around this time, but ME3 ended up feeling like another brainless sequel to a previously thought-provoking series. Even the music sucks because Jack Wall, the lead composer of the previous two games, is gone and they replaced him with TV show composers instead.

The only saving grace of this game is the combat and that shines the best in the multiplayer. It's a simple concept: co-op wave horde shooter where you get credits for completing objectives. These credits can be spent on a variety of gacha crates to unlock weapon upgrades, mods, consumables, and even new characters. You start with only male and female vanilla versions of the ME3 classes, but later you can unlock characters with unique skills for each class. There's still an active community on this 13 years later, but you might have to find some friends to enjoy the grind. I'm stuck in this awkward spot now where my gear is too strong for Bronze difficulty, but I struggle to solo in Silver. It's very addictive and a lot of fun, it's just a shame that the disastrous single player campaign is attached to it.

I don't understand what happened to this game because all three games have almost the same upper staff. This was the first game where EA had full publishing control, so maybe their meddling forced it out the door along with all the bad changes to the game. Maybe it was Casey Hudson biting off more than he could chew and realizing they "had" to push out the final game of the trilogy before the end of the console cycle. Regardless, this game is a dumpster fire that is only carried by it's improved gameplay and multiplayer. Unless you want to grind MP with friends, avoid this game completely. I wish I could play a standalone client for MP so I'm not clocking more hours into this embarrassing mess on Steam.

Very nostalgic game for me, I loved Mass Effect 2 and then played this shortly after many many years ago and can remember it as being very fun and entertaining. But I think Playing it now more than 10 years later can suck for some people use to cry high graphics games and game mechanics, But the combat for me isn't as bad. Plus you are more after the rich story telling experience, and that is what made me hooked way back then. I hope if they ever make a new Mass Effect game that is will be as good as Mass Effect 3 or better.

the multiplayer/coop mode is surprisingly underrated, absolutely worth it just for that. surprisingly high skill ceiling, even aside from the jank, and a wide variety of playstyles/characters and insane levels of power fantasy. not many games where you can play as a spec ops ryu hayabusa with space magic or a huge alien frog bruiser headbutting and hammering everything in sight. really f*cking cringe that they didnt port it over for the "legendary" edition which is anything but. feels good to write a quick ode to a MP mode ive put a lot of time into (many hours on origin, not listed here) ive been a big fan of for a very long time.

only issue is a lot of the progression takes place via credits purchasing lootboxes alongside character leveling... this doesn't matter though as bioware barely exists anymore and you can easily cheat for whatever characters/weapons you want, and i highly recommend doing so. also consider using the very new unofficial MP patch https://www.nexusmods.com/masseffect3/mods/1040
